question: You used a Claude Code session to analyze why your customer support agent mishandles billing disputes, reading the tool descriptions of lookup_order and process_refund and twenty disputed-charge conversations. You now want to try two divergent fixes: rewriting both tool descriptions to state when each tool applies, and splitting dispute handling into a prompt chain with a separate verification pass. Each fix should start from the shared analysis, and work on one fix should not shape the other. What should you do?

options.text: Start a new session for each fix that names only the fix, and have each session begin its work without the earlier analysis.
options.reason: Each new session loses the shared analysis baseline, so neither fix builds on the investigation of the tool descriptions and disputed-charge conversations.

options.text: Save the analysis findings in a scratchpad file, and then explore both fixes one after the other in the analysis session.
options.reason: The scratchpad keeps the findings, but both fixes still share one conversation, so work on the first fix shapes the second; there are no independent branches.

options.text: Use /memory to add the analysis findings to the project CLAUDE.md, and then explore both fixes together in the analysis session.
options.reason: Exploring both fixes in the same conversation lets each one influence the other, which is the opposite of the independent branches that fork_session gives.

options.text: Use fork_session on the analysis session to create two branches, and then explore one fix in each branch from the shared baseline.
options.reason: fork_session creates independent branches from a shared analysis baseline, so each divergent fix starts from the same analysis without influencing the other.
